questions.q: What did Bruce Lee refuse to do with his own martial art, Jeet Kune Do?
a: Formalize it, so each student could interpret it their own way
Teach it to students outside Chinese communities
Combine it with the Wing Chun forms he had learned
Write it down in a published training manual
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Lee kept Jeet Kune Do unformalized so every student would find their own understanding.

questions.q: What does the instruction to 'empty your cup' mean?
a: Approach new situations without preconceived opinions
Fill your mind with as much knowledge as possible
Learn from one teacher rather than from many
Practice a skill until it becomes automatic
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a mind already full of opinions has no room left for new insight, so keep a beginner's mind.

questions.q: Which story does Lee use to explain emptying your cup?
a: A Zen teacher pouring tea until the visitor's cup overflows
A boat drifting quietly in Hong Kong harbor
A student who refuses to spar with his teacher
A master who splits a stone by striking water
questions.why: Lesson 2 retells the tea story, where the teacher keeps pouring to show the visitor's mind is already full.

questions.q: Why does lesson 3 hold up water as a model for how to live?
a: It adapts to any container while still reaching its goal
It always takes the shortest and most direct route
It stays perfectly calm whatever it meets
It wears down every obstacle slowly over time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says water takes whatever path is open and so arrives exactly where it is meant to be.

questions.q: Where did Lee's insight about being like water come from?
a: Punching the water while lying in a drifting boat as a teenager
Watching a river flood near his first martial arts school
A lesson from his teacher Ip Man over a cup of tea
A scene he performed in one of his Hong Kong films
questions.why: The overview describes Lee striking the harbor water during a week off and seeing that it simply moved aside.
